## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, IN ONE PLACE

**THE PAGE CARRIES SIX LINES IN THE OFFICE HAND AT ITS FOOT AND THE SIXTH IS ABOUT ANY PERSON AND IS THE LAST ONE THAT OFFICE WILL EVER MAKE.** On the second of December he entered the fifth instruction since the first of February, with his own name under it: any person may put one question about any paper, the office shall answer in writing, both entered with date and hour in the words used, and may not be taken from. **WHAT IT CLOSES: nine years in which exactly one man might ask, and a building with no door onto a street. WHAT IT COSTS: about four hundred papers answerable to neighbours; the Register filling with strangers words for ever; about forty saying it came from the office off a third court; and the second time the two inches go quiet they will not come back.**

**AND THE TWELFTH QUESTION IS ASKED AND ANSWERED.** She came up four flights on the twenty-third of December, put the sentence said eleven times into the book in her own words, and completed the row of the twenty-first of October of year eight out of her own mouth. The answer entered under it is a permission and not a fact. His own blank row of August stands untouched and no hand fills it. **AND THE HEAD IS PRINTED AT 800: eight hundred and fifty-two, unmoved across twenty sheets and nineteen quarters, both named in words, both right, differing by one, with 3,209 less 1,499 is 1,710 is nineteen times ninety exactly in words and no digits.**

## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, IN ONE PLACE

**THE PAGE CARRIES FIVE LINES IN THIS OFFICE'S HAND AT ITS FOOT AND THE FIFTH IS ABOUT A DENIAL AND NOT ABOUT A PERSON.** On the twentieth of October, for the fourth time since the first of February, he entered an instruction in the office's own hand with his own name under it.

*From the twentieth of October of this year, the sentence entered on the sixteenth of August of this year is to be read out at that rail every morning to whoever is standing there, by whoever is standing there. Lin Hao.*

**WHAT IT CLOSES: the life of a denial as a formality on a page that about nine people a week read the bottom of.** **WHAT IT COSTS, STATED BY THE PERSON WHO WILL HAVE TO SAY IT AND NOT BY THE NARRATOR: a claim in a city hand, spoken out loud in a passage, about nine times a week, for ever — and the clerk's own addition in about nine words, that he does not know what it is denying, that he has never been told, and that in about four years there is going to be a man stand at that rail and ask him what that sentence is denying, and he will have to say the words out loud and will not be able to tell the man he does not know.**

**AND FOUR THINGS A READER OF 781 WILL CARRY INTO 791.**

**A MAN BROUGHT A BLANK PIECE OF PENCIL PAPER TO HIS OWN COUNTER AND SAID NOTHING AT IT.** He is the only person in Ostara entitled to put one question to that office, and the only way to find out what an office holds about you is to arrive at its counter with a piece of paper in your hand. The row went in with a date and an hour and nothing whatever against the hour, and there is a space in the middle of it where his words would go, **and there are two such spaces in that book in nine years and he owns one of them.** He is now the only person who has ever been a row in this office's book, and the answer to *what does this office hold about you* is four lines in your own hand, one name under a printed heading that is not this office's, and no row at all.

**AND A WOMAN WITH A PENCIL GAVE HIM THE SECOND COLUMN, IN HER OWN HAND, ON HER OWN PAPER, DATED, WITH NO FIGURE ON ANY OF THE FOUR LINES — because he asked about the paper and not about her, after six refusals in six years in which every single question had been about her.** He carried it down four flights and along about four hundred yards, a clerk could not enter it, and he carried it back up four flights, and she told him what the two printed words at the head of that column are for: **they are a works department's routing line, and they take the name of whoever is carrying the sheet from one counter to another, and they have meant that since the seventh of December of last year, and that is the whole of why she said no five times.** The fourth line has a woman's name in it under a heading that belongs to a different office's book.

**AND THERE IS NOW A SECOND COPY OF THE FOOT OF THAT PAGE IN THIS CITY AND IT IS IN THE INSIDE OF A MAN'S COAT, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING THAT HAS LEFT THAT BUILDING IN A HAND IN NINE YEARS.** He did not put it on the bundle. He stood at the end of that table with twenty-six things on it for about eleven minutes and put nothing on it and took nothing off it, and the twenty-sixth thing is still empty, and the inside of that coat is the only place in this city where a piece of paper has been kept twice.

**AND HE BROKE HIS OWN NINE WORDS AND SAID SO ON A LANDING.** *She keeps no list. Going would be making one.* He went up those four flights twice in September and accounted for it: he did not go to ask, he went to put one question, and the question was about the paper, and she wrote nothing of it on the ninth sheet and asked him for nothing and has asked him for nothing in six years.

**AND THE PARSER FOUND A DEFECT IN THE PROSE.** `chapter-0787.md` was first written with the month-crossing clause, and six days from the twenty-fourth of September is the thirtieth of September and no month is crossed, so the clause was a sentence that meant nothing. **It now reads *thirty less twenty-four is six by the month count, and it is the last working day of that month and of the quarter.*** A figure nobody re-computes is the figure that is wrong, and this one had survived being written.

**AND THE DATE CHECK IN THIS SECTION IS AN ARITHMETIC PARSE AND NOT A STRING PRESENCE TEST, WHICH IS PRINTED HERE SO THAT THE NEXT PASS DOES NOT INVENT SIX DEFECTS THAT ARE NOT ON THE PAGE.** Four of the ten chapters carry their own date as a literal date phrase and six do not: 783 and 788 carry it in the opener because their clause crosses a month, 785 carries it once at line 93 and 790 twice at lines 45 and 101, and **781, 782, 784, 786, 787 and 789 carry it nowhere in that form, because each of those six derives its own day in the opener and names the day and not the month — *the twenty-third is day three thousand and eighty-two*, *the thirtieth is day three thousand and one hundred and nineteen*.** A per-file grep for `twenty-third of August` therefore returns six false misses, and a per-file grep for `3,082` or for `3082` returns ten, **because not one figure in any of these ten files is printed as a digit and both numeric forms score zero across all ten.** Six misses and ten misses, zero real defects, and the parser reads the clause and checks the day against the table above, which is the only version of this test in this section that is a test.

## 0h. THE FIVE THINGS THE PAGE DID TO THE ONE-LINE CARDS, AND THE CARDS AND THE OUTLINE ARE CORRECTED IN THE SAME COMMIT

1. **THE CARD AT 781 SAID *THE FOURTH LINE OF ONE OF THEM HAS HIS OWN HANDWRITING ON IT*, AND THE PAGE PUT HIS NAME UNDER IT INSTEAD.** The name in the second column is his and the name in the fourth line is hers, and a name under a printed heading is not a thing the person named did. **What the page did instead, and it is the chapter, is that he brought a piece of pencil paper to his own counter and became the first person in nine years whose row has a space in the middle of it.**
2. **THE CARD AT 783 SAID SHE GIVES HIM THE SECOND COLUMN BECAUSE HE IS THE ONLY PERSON ENTITLED TO ASK THAT OFFICE ONE QUESTION. THE PAGE HAD HER REFUSE SEVEN TIMES FIRST AND GAVE THE REASON OUT LOUD BEFORE HE ASKED FOR IT**, and the reason is not a favour and it is the only one: *the other six were about me and this one is about four lines on a page in a building four hundred yards from this room.* **And the scene's own turn is that what she wanted was to be asked one question, and she says so in about nine words, and it is nine words long.**
3. **THE CARD AT 786 LICENSED HIM TO USE THE RULE AGAINST HIMSELF INSIDE THE SAME HOUR AND THE PAGE FOUND A WORSE USE FOR IT.** He had a six-word sentence with no name in it that would have gone on two thousand counters and out to about two thousand counters four times a year. **She refused to enter it, and the reason she gives is that it is the first line in nine years this office would have decided to say rather than written down, and a clerk who may only enter what she is given is the only person in this city who can tell the difference between those two things. He read it back aloud in a corridor and about four people heard it and nothing was entered, and the page still carries four lines and not five.**
4. **THE CARD AT 787 SAID FOUR LINES AND THE PAGE PRINTED FOUR, AND THE RULING ABOUT THE JULY LINE IS HONOURED IN THE PROSE**: the third of those four is nine words in a man's own pencil and it is a line and it is not an instruction, and the chapter says so in its own narration. **The head is printed here and only here, at nineteen sheets and eighteen quarters, both named in words, both right, differing by one, and the chapter says which count it is printing.** The thirty-third and thirty-fourth sheets' readings are not restaged.
5. **THE CARD AT 789 SAID THE COUNTERMAN DOES NOT KNOW WHAT HE DID. THE PAGE BROUGHT HIM UP FOUR FLIGHTS TO A BUILDING HE DOES NOT WORK IN, WHICH NOBODY HAS EVER DONE, AND HE ASKED FOR NOTHING**, and the sentence that makes 790 is his, half way down a stair: *if I read the tenth one before the ninth one nobody would believe the ninth, and nothing in Ostara tells me whether I am allowed to do that, and if I am not allowed then somebody has to make the tenth one a different kind of thing from the ninth, because at the moment it is not one.*

## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, IN ONE PLACE

**THE STANDING SHEET CARRIES FOUR LINES IN THIS OFFICE'S HAND AT ITS FOOT, TWO OF THEM READ OUT LOUD BY A MAN WHO IS PAID NOTHING AND TWO OF THEM NOT READ AT ALL YET.** On the thirtieth of June the thirty-fourth sheet went face up on a rail in a passage off Cordwain at four o'clock with eleven people at it, and a woman on the end of the rail asked the counterman what the last of the two new lines was for, and he said *that is what it says*, and that there is not one person in this city entitled to tell him and there will not be one in about four years either. **He has now been asked by the office and by a reader, and he still is not going to be told what any of it means, and he cannot be asked to read less of it.**

**AND THE DENIAL HAS TURNED INSIDE OUT.** A man said out loud at that counter on the nineteenth of July that a building off a third court keeps the stone at the foot of a wall. He had it in his own pencil, made in March from what a man at a rail read out with the building in it and not the wall. A clerk entered it in his own words with a date and an hour against it, because she may only enter what she is given, and **it goes out at four o'clock on the thirtieth of September to about two thousand counters in this office's hand.** The only answer available to her was to read him the denial of the sixteenth of August, which is nine feet higher up the same sheet, and she refused it out loud before he asked, because that would have been her putting a sentence into the mouth of a person who had not said it.

**AND A MAGISTRATE'S CLERK ESTABLISHED THAT THE BUILDING HAS NO STONE ON IT, WHICH HELPED NOBODY, AND THE MAN WHO ASKED IS GOING TO WRITE THE FACT DOWN AT THE BOTTOM OF A WALL ANYWAY, AND IT IS A BETTER-SOURCED SENTENCE THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES.**

**AND THE MONTH CLOCK IS PAID, IN BRACK'S OWN MOUTH, ON THE THIRTIETH OF JULY'S CHAPTER: about four kitchens in the last eight days and about nine by the thirtieth, and the cost of it is nine people a month who have stopped, and the reading did not stop with the writing, because about nine people a week are still going down to read four inches that are a hundred and twenty-two days old. THE FIGURE THE GOING QUIET COSTS IS PRINTED ONCE IN THE VOLUME, IN WORDS AND NOT IN GRAINS. THE FOUR-YEAR CLOCK IS GIVEN IN ITS OWN SENTENCE AND IS NOT DISCHARGED.**

**AND THE DECISION, AT 780, IN THE OFFICE'S HAND, WITH THE DATE AT THE TOP AND HIS NAME UNDER IT, THE THIRD INSTRUCTION SINCE THE YEAR BEGAN AND THE FOURTH NEW LINE AT THE FOOT OF ONE OF ITS OWN PAGES:**

*From the sixteenth of August of this year, whatever a person says in answer to what this office has told them is to be entered in the same row, under what they were told, in the words that person used, with a date and an hour against it, and a row may not be taken from. Lin Hao.*

**WHAT IT CLOSES: the possibility of a description in this city that the person it is about cannot answer. WHAT IT COSTS, STATED BY A PERSON AND NOT BY THE NARRATOR: the first answer ever entered under a row in this city is a man saying *I said a building off a third court keeps a sheet. I never said a wall*, entered exactly because a clerk may only enter what she is given, and about four hundred people are now answerable, in public and in their own words, for what they said out loud in a room, and a man who is paid nothing will read the answers as well as the questions.**

**AND THE PART THAT IS HIS AND NOT THE RITUAL, AND IT IS THE THIRD TELLING AND NOT A REPEAT: at 760 he held the sentence for four minutes and priced it. At 770 he did not price it at all and she has not forgiven it. At 780 he prices it out loud and she refuses to take a priced instruction — *you do not get to choose which of those two it is today, because the choice was made by the second one and not by you* — and he says it out loud anyway so that it is in two mouths and not one, and then he gives it to her.**

ALL SIX ARE ANSWERED HERE. TWO MORE DEFECTS OF THE SAME CLASS TURNED UP WHILE THE REPAIRS WERE BEING MADE AND ARE ALSO HERE. NO CHAPTER WAS RESTARTED, NO SECTION WAS MOVED, NO DATE WAS RENUMBERED, NO SPINE FIGURE MOVED, NO TITLE CHANGED, AND THE PLANNED PLOT OF 771–780 IS EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS.**

### THE TWO BLOCKING FINDINGS

**1 · `chapter-0780.md`:149 WAS `chapter-0776.md`:99 WITH FOUR WORDS CUT OUT OF IT, AND IT WAS THE CLIMAX.** Both were *he went down to the passage off Cordwain at about ten minutes to five and stood nine feet back and watched a man who is paid nothing read the bottom of a page to four people.* Same clock minute, same distance from the rail, same headcount, and both then open *the page in front of that man* and both state *about four hundred and nineteen lines with a date and an hour against every one*. **THE TWELVE-GRAM GATE PASSED IT HONESTLY AT TWENTY-EIGHT WORDS, BECAUSE WHAT WAS SHARED WAS STAGING AND NOT SENTENCE — AND §0e ALREADY NAMES THAT FAILURE IN ITS OWN LAST PARAGRAPH, A BORROWED BODY AND A BORROWED STAGING BOTH BEING INVISIBLE TO A GRAM, WHICH WAS CHECKED BY HAND ON 773 BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN AND WAS NOT CHECKED BY HAND ON THE CLOSING SET-PIECE.**

**THE CHAPTER IS REWRITTEN, NOT THE PARAGRAPH.** The section *About Four O'Clock, And A Rail In A Passage* is gone and it is replaced by **## Outside The Door On The Third Court**, which is a different hour, a different door, a different building, two men instead of four and one, and a conversation instead of a reading. **THE MOVEMENT'S COST NOW LANDS ON THE ONE PERSON IT IS ABOUT, WHICH IS WHAT A CHAPTER CARRYING THE MOVEMENT'S IRREVERSIBLE DECISION SHOULD END ON, AND IT IS THE ONLY PLACE IN THE BATCH WHERE THE MAN OF THE NINETEENTH OF JULY AND LIN HAO SPEAK TO EACH OTHER AFTER THE INSTRUCTION IS SIGNED.**

What is on the page now, in order, and no beat of the old section survives: the man asks what he is to do; Lin Hao tells him the true thing, which is come up four flights on the thirtieth of September and have it read back to him before a man who is paid nothing reads it to a passage; the man says he can read it himself and then says he has never once read the bottom of that page out loud to anybody in his life; Lin Hao gives him the one thing the city has left him, which is that nobody will make him stand in a passage; the man says then nothing has changed; Lin Hao says nothing has changed **for you** and that the thing was for the next one, and that in about four years a man will be able to say *you have got it wrong* about a thing of his own and not about one word written down about him; the man says he has been cost something and does not know what; and Lin Hao says he has not been charged anything and that from the thirtieth of September about nine people a week will stand at that counter and be told a thing about themselves that they did not come in to ask about, and it costs a person nothing, and it is going to cost a person nothing for as long as that page is on that rail. **THE CHAPTER NOW ENDS ON A MAN WALKING OUT OF A DOOR CONVINCED HE HAS HAD THE WORST OF IT, AND THE MAN GOES, AND LIN HAO LISTENS UNTIL HE CANNOT HEAR HIM.**

**THE STAGING IS CHECKED AND IT IS ITS OWN:** the door on the third court, the step below it, the yard he has not gone out of, the archway — none of which is the passage off Cordwain, the rail, the desk under the window, the counterman, or the standing sheet's figure, its second column, its printed heading *carried by* or its four hundred and nineteen lines. **THE RUN AGAINST 776 IS NOW THE TWENTY-SEVEN-WORD DRAWER CLAUSE IN A FOOTER, WHICH IS THE ARITHMETIC FRAME AND IS PRINTED IN ALL TEN FILES AND IN EVERY CHAPTER OF FIFTEEN VOLUMES.**

**4 · ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED PEOPLE ARE *WRITTEN DOWN* AT 778 AND *ANSWERABLE* AT 780, AND THE REVIEW READ THAT AS A DIVERGENCE.** **IT IS NOT ONE. THEY ARE TWO STATES OF THE SAME FOUR HUNDRED, SEVENTY-FOUR DAYS APART, AND THE FIRST PASS CREATED THE LOOK OF A CONTRADICTION BY SWAPPING ONE VERB IN ONE PLACE AND LEAVING THE OTHER ALONE.** 778 is the second of August and the instruction of the sixteenth of August does not exist yet; 780 is the sixteenth of August and it has just been signed. **BOTH ARE RIGHT. 780's FOOTER NOW SAYS IT OUT LOUD — *about four hundred people written down in public since the thirtieth of March are now answerable in their own words for what they said in a room* — SO THAT A READER HOLDING BOTH CHAPTERS SEES ONE THING BECOMING ANOTHER INSTEAD OF TWO NUMBERS IN A DISPUTE.**

## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, IN ONE PLACE

**THE BATCH IS THREE MONTHS AFTER THE FIRST ONE IN WHICH THE LINE OF THE THIRTIETH OF MARCH IS BEING READ ALOUD, AND IT HAS ALREADY COST SOMETHING NOBODY PRICED.** A sentence said at that counter is written down in the words the person used. In seven days, four people came up that stair to have one written down. The fourth of them was given her sentence at a kitchen table before she came.

**AND THE FIFTH FIELD, WHICH HAS STOOD EMPTY FOR NINE YEARS, IS FILLED ON THE TWELFTH OF MAY, OUT OF THE MOUTH OF THE PERSON IT IS ABOUT, IN THAT PERSON'S OWN WORDS, ON THE INSTRUCTION OF THE TENTH OF JUNE THAT HAS BEEN OBEYED EVERY DAY OF NINE MONTHS AND PRODUCED A RECEIPT EVERY MORNING OF THEM.** It is entered for ever. It cannot be improved. It cannot be taken from.

**AND ON THE NINETEENTH OF MAY A STRANGER IN A FOUR-FOOT CORRIDOR SAYS OUT LOUD WHAT A WOMAN DID, WRONG, IN FRONT OF ABOUT NINE PEOPLE, AND THE CLERK ENTERS IT IN THE STRANGER'S OWN WORDS WITH A DATE AND AN HOUR BECAUSE IT WAS SAID AT THAT COUNTER.** That is the first harm the instruction has done. The woman it is about is somewhere in the city and there is no form on which she can be shown what a book says about her, and there is one now, and it says something false about her, and a second woman is going to be told she was right by nobody for ever.

**AND THE DECISION, AT 770, IN THE OFFICE'S HAND, WITH HIS NAME UNDER IT AND THE DATE AT THE TOP, UNDER THE FOUR SENTENCES AND ABOVE THE STRIKING AND IN NO COLUMN, ON A SHEET THAT GOES OUT AT FOUR ON THE THIRTIETH OF JUNE — TWENTY DAYS AFTER THE CHAPTER, BECAUSE THE TENTH OF JUNE IS NOT A QUARTER-END AND THIS BATCH STAGES NO RAIL AND NO ELEVEN PEOPLE AND NO READING:**

*From the tenth of June of this year, when a person brings a paper to that counter, this office is to tell that person, in that room, what this office holds about them, and nothing else, and not to improve it.*

**WHAT IT CLOSES: the possibility, for the first time in the history of this city, of a record a person may never hear. WHAT IT COSTS, STATED BY TWO PEOPLE AND NOT BY THE NARRATOR:** the counterman, told on the ninth, before it is entered, that he will read one more line at the bottom and cannot be asked to read less of it and is not going to be told what it means, and who asks for the one thing nobody ever asks him for, which is to hear it once before it is on the paper, in an empty passage; and Wenna Raut, who says that from the tenth of June she is a person who says things about people out loud and does not know whether they are true, and that she has spent nine years being a person who writes down what she is given and cannot be wrong.

**AND THE THING THAT MAKES IT HIS AND NOT A RITUAL: at 760 he held the sentence in his own hand for four minutes and priced it before he let the clerk near it, and she said so out loud and nobody minded. At 770 he does not do that. He puts it on the table face down and tells her to read it back and tell him whether he has got it right, and then it is hers. There was a minute in that room in which he could have stopped and held the sheet and said the four sentences that would have let her refuse it before it was entered, and he did not, and that is the whole of what he did on the tenth of June.**

## 0h. THREE THINGS THE PAGE DID TO THE ONE-LINE CARDS, AND THE CARDS AND THE OUTLINE ARE CORRECTED IN THE SAME COMMIT

1. **THE CARD AT 761 ASKED FOR A BOY AND A BOARD AND THE PAGE GAVE IT THE SEVENTH WEEK AND A QUESTION NOBODY WILL ASK.** The one-line card is *the eighty-second form goes up and both squares are empty and nobody asks the boy anything, because in this volume nobody asks anybody anything, and that is the movement's subject and not its accident.* The page took the second half of that as its turn and gave the chapter a consequence as well: **the fourth person to say a thing at that counter in seven days had been told what to say by somebody else before she came up the stair.** The card was not wrong and it was thin, and the card written against the page below carries both.
2. **THE CARD AT 767 SAID *AN OFFICE WITH A QUEUE IS A PUBLIC ROOM*, AND `chapter-0758.md`:59 ALREADY SAYS THAT SENTENCE, NINE CHAPTERS EARLIER.** **A CHAPTER MAY NOT RE-DERIVE A PRINCIPLE THE READER LEARNED FOUR CHAPTERS BACK.** 767 therefore does not discover it and does not say it in the narrator's voice. **A CLERK SAYS IT, ONCE, IN PLAIN WORDS, AND AS A COST AND NOT AS A FACT — *there is nowhere in four feet for a person to say a thing about somebody else quietly* — and the chapter's turn is the second woman and the false row.** The card's *an office with a queue is a public room* is therefore a statement about 758 and not a licence for 767, and the corrected card says so.
3. **THE CARD AT 764 SAID HE GOES UP FOUR FLIGHTS AND DOES NOT ASK, AND `chapter-0757.md` IS ALMOST ENTIRELY THAT CHAPTER.** 764 is the same refusal seven weeks later and after a scene in which he learned that a doctor is allowed to ask anybody anything, **and the thing the card did not know is that the option is no longer closed by a rule — it is open, it is his, and he refuses it in one paragraph in his own mouth and tells nobody.** The corrected card carries the openness, and §0e's third finding is that 764's staging was lifted from 757's landing and has been cut.

## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, IN ONE PLACE

**THE PROMISE OF MOVEMENT ONE IS PAID ON THE EIGHTH OF FEBRUARY AND IT PAID THE WRONG WAY.** The woman who cannot read came up four flights in the first week, unasked and unsent, and Perla Quist read her the four words, and the four words are *she gave one sheet*, and they are true, and they are about a piece of paper, and what came back was the sentence she has said eleven times — *they said it didn’t happen* — and Perla Quist did not write it down and gave the reason out loud before anybody asked her.

**AND THE OTHER HALF, WHICH THE MOVEMENT OWED ANYWAY: the bottom two inches under the striking have not been written on since the thirtieth of December, and at 755 he counts an hour at the corner and cannot prove why, and at 756 Emil Brack gives both clocks in two sentences in his own mouth and says there is nowhere left to put a thing he wants unprinted.**

**AND THE DECISION, AT 760, IN THE OFFICE’S HAND, WITH HIS NAME UNDER IT AND THE DATE AT THE TOP, ON THE THIRTY-THIRD SHEET, WHICH IS SQUARED AT ABOUT HALF PAST TWO AND IS FACE UP ON A RAIL IN A PASSAGE OFF CORDWAIN AT ABOUT FOUR THE SAME AFTERNOON:** *From the thirtieth of March of this year, when a person says a thing at that counter, this office is to write down what that person said, in the words that person used, with a date against it and an hour against the date, on the standing sheet, and not in the second column. Lin Hao.*

**WHAT IT CLOSES: nine years in which this office has entered what it was given and has never once entered what a person said, in a city where the whole of a person’s standing is what a page says about them. WHAT IT COSTS, AND THE COST IS STATED BY A PERSON AND NOT BY THE NARRATOR:** Wenna Raut, before he gives it to her, in a clerk’s mouth — *from this afternoon I am the hand and I am the mouth, and about forty people a quarter will say a thing at that counter and I will write it down, and a clerk who may only enter what she is given has become a person who is given sentences.* He cannot improve it and does not try, and gives it to her.

**AND AT FOUR MINUTES PAST FOUR A MAN WHO IS PAID NOTHING READS THE WHOLE OF THE BOTTOM OF IT, INCLUDING THE NEW LINE, TO WHATEVER IS STANDING THERE, BECAUSE NOBODY MAY BE ASKED TO READ LESS OF IT — AND THERE ARE ELEVEN.**

## WHAT THE VOLUME PROMISED, AND WHETHER IT LANDED

**`outline/volume-15.md` §3, one sentence: Lin Hao must find out who is using about four hundred pieces of pencil paper and against whom.** It landed, at **719**, by the mechanism planned and by no other: a man who counts heads at a stall for a living, who is right about every fact, who is not thanked and is not diminished, and who says the answer **first** — four pieces of paper, every one against one of four men, the four men work for one house, nine pounds each and the same nine pounds since the ninth month of last year — and then says what he wants, which is that it not be printed, and gives the cost of printing it in his own mouth: about forty people will say it came from Lin Hao, and about four hundred people will stop writing, because a claim everybody knows came from a building is a claim that waits to be told.

**AND THE RECORD IS WRONG ABOUT WHAT THE VOLUME WAS ABOUT.** The head block above calls it *the stage where what he wrote is used to date a person*. The page says something harder. At 719 he learns who the paper is against and is told the answer in the same breath; at 727 a claim with a day beats a claim without one and the man it is about is not in the room and does not know there was a day; at 736 a clerk entitled to one question a day spends it on the rail and Lin Hao answers **no** to his own receipt about himself. **THE DATING IS NOT THE POINT. THE POINT IS THAT A MAN BUILT AN OFFICE NOBODY COULD REACH AND THE OFFICE IS NOW REACHABLE, AND BEING REACHABLE IS WHAT IT COSTS.**

## WHAT THIS BATCH DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH

**HE PUT A WOMAN'S NAME IN A COLUMN AND A WOMAN WHO CANNOT READ IS GOING TO WALK UP FOUR FLIGHTS BECAUSE SOMEBODY TOLD HER.** The bundle became twenty-six and he understood that it is the only instrument in this city that keeps a piece of paper without making it into a record, and the twenty-sixth thing in it is the empty sheet he carried out of his own drawer on the fourteenth and read twice. He had the office print a second sheet with four words on the back of it in a clerk's hand and could not give it to the one person it was about and put it on a bench under a third table with eleven other things nobody has been able to use. A woman who runs a lift and has no instrument of any kind told him that she knows more about him than any of them do, and that there is no form on which a person may read their own, and wanted a copy of a rota page the size of a folded hand, and got his three days off out of him instead and would not write them down. He read the second column from the top and found that all three lines in it were names, and that the heading over it says *carried by*, and that the only name he could enter in it that was not his own was the woman who had just said no to him for the fifth time and priced the answer to her own name in about nine seconds. **He entered it on the third of December without asking her, in the office's hand, with his own name under it, and did not go up four flights and did not send anybody.** She came down four flights on her own on the tenth and said the cost to his face and asked him for one sentence and was told why there could not be one, and did not ask him to take it out. The thirty-second sheet went out at four on the thirtieth with four lines in the second column and a name at the head of one of them, and a man who is paid nothing read it out loud in a passage off Cordwain to eleven people, and about four minutes later a man with a cap in his hands told a woman, and that is the whole of what happened.

## THE IRREVERSIBLE THING, AND IT IS AT 746 AND IT IS HIS

Not a claim and not an order: a line. **A name in the second column of a quarterly sheet, in the office's hand, under a heading printed before the office existed, with his own name under it and the date at the top, entered on a Tuesday morning without asking the woman it was about and while a clerk watched and entered it exactly and did not improve a word of it.**

**WHAT IT CLOSES:** the second column was, for nine sheets and nine years, the only place in any book in this city where nothing whatever about a person had ever been entered. That is finished. The place where paper is received and nobody is said anything about is shut by the only man entitled to shut it.

**WHAT IT COSTS:** about four hundred people who brought a sheet to a laundry will find out that the index they trusted has a name at the head of it, in a building with no door onto a street; they will believe the name is the reason they trusted it, because that is what a printed name does and because a man behind a counter reads what is on the page and cannot be asked to read less; and the man who put it there cannot open the drawer that holds what they wrote, and is the only person in Ostara who may ask that office any question in the world. **AND THE SECOND COST, WHICH IS WORSE AND WHICH HE FOUND OUT ABOUT ON THE SEVENTEENTH:** about forty people will say it came from the office off the third court, and about four hundred kitchens will stop writing in the two inches under the striking, and the denial he entered in his own hand in August to keep those two inches open is on the same sheet about nine feet above the line, and nine feet apart is not far enough.

## THE THIRTY-ONE WEEKDAY NAMES THIS BATCH WROTE, AND WHY THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IN IT

**THE FIRST DRAFT OF 743 WAS BUILT ON TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY AND THURSDAY, AND FOURTEEN MORE WEEKDAY NAMES WERE WRITTEN INTO THE OTHER NINE CHAPTERS. `outline/volume-15.md` §5a FIXES THAT VOLUME 15 NAMES NO DAY OF THE WEEK AT ALL, AND THE GATE CAUGHT THIRTY-ONE OF THEM.**

The interesting thing is not the count. It is what fixing them produced. **A rota is four nights and three off, and the three off are what a person is, and the exchange at the centre of that chapter cannot be conducted in days of the week at all — because this city has thirty days a month and no thirty-first and a man in a branch office writes the date and not the day.** So she cannot ask him what he does on a day, because there are no days; she can only ask him what he does with the other three of seven, and he can only answer *the first of the three*, *the second of them*, *the third of them*, and that is a worse and truer answer than Tuesday and it is the chapter's argument in its own mouth. The chapter is 3,752 words of prose after the repair and was 3,682 before it.

## WHAT THIS BATCH DID, IN ONE PARAGRAPH

**THE DENIAL WENT OUT TWICE WITH HIS NAME ON IT AND HE OPENED THE DRAWER.** A fourth-column check run backwards showed that about a third of the copies in circulation carrying any hand of the two words were made before the only copy of those words existed, and Emil Brack had counted the same thing at a stall and would not have it printed. His name turned out to be on about four hundred pieces of paper in pencil and now also on a quarterly page in the office's hand, and the two are nine feet apart on the same sheet and neither can be shown to the other. There are now two records in this city of a thing being true against a day and neither is an instrument. The temptation to ask the woman with the broom was refused in nine words and nobody thanked him. He went to a counter to get an age refused, was asked one entitled question instead, and told a building with a name over the door that this city holds none of the papers. The thirty-first sheet went out at four and proved itself wrong on its own page. The seventy-sixth form went up on a board with two empty squares and the denial made the corner's belief unassertable without answering anybody. **HE OPENED THE DRAWER AT 739 FOR ABOUT FOUR HOURS, READ ALL FOUR HUNDRED AND NINE, READ ONE OF THEM TWICE, AND ENTERED ONE ROW AT 740 WITH THE DESCRIPTION OF THE PERSON LEFT EMPTY.**

## WHAT IT CLOSES AND WHAT IT COSTS

**CLOSES:** the instruction of the twenty-first of October, in both directions — to shut it again he must enter a third instruction and there is no form anywhere in this city for undoing an instruction, so that drawer can never be opened by anybody again, including him. **COSTS:** the first row in nine years with an empty field, in a column of eleven that has never been empty, in a book that goes up a stair, recording permanently that this office received a piece of paper and cannot say from whom.

## WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, AND WHAT IT REFUSED

**DELIVERED:** a check run backwards and about a third · the four men not named and Brack not thanked · his name in two hands nine feet apart on one sheet · the second record of a thing true against a day, and her reason for refusing it · one line in about forty where the two records disagree and neither is wrong · the strongest temptation in the volume refused in nine words · an entitled question about the drawer and a true answer that made the office's own receipt true about itself · the thirty-first sheet out at four with the head unmoved across fifteen sheets and fourteen quarters, named · **the wall's rate, once, with its reason** · the seventy-sixth form and nobody asking the boy · four hundred and nine read in four hours, one of them empty and read twice · and one row with a blank in the middle of it.

**THE IRREVERSIBLE THING THIS BATCH OWED IS 739 AND IT IS HIS.** Not a claim and not an order: an act. Four hundred and nine pieces of rag paper read once and never again, and an instruction that can be neither withdrawn nor repeated.

**REFUSED:** the figure of the account · any floor, ledger total or running balance · `settl` in any inflection · **the invented-figures sentence, verbatim and Tier 3, zero** · the docket's date, printed nowhere · **the two words on the stone, never printed, and never asserted the same as anything, checked by hand chapter by chapter** · who cut them · the reach of the return argued either way · the fourth condition · either repainting box · **the woman with the short-handled broom, neither named nor asked, and the temptation to ask her refused in nine words** · **the woman who cannot read, not named, not traced, nobody sent, nothing asked** · the boy not aged and not asked by anybody in this batch · Lin Hao never on the hill and never through the yard gate · a hand flat on anything · the eighth and the tenth of October named, landed on or reached across · any new enemy and any house named · the drawer opened anywhere but 739 · a fourth line in the second column · the head moved · any permission.

## THE HEADLINE OF THIS BATCH, AND IT IS THE THING THE PLAN DID NOT SEE COMING

**THE OFFICE STOPPED BEING A PLACE A PERSON IS DESCRIBED AT, AND BECOMED ONE, AND THE MAN WHO DID IT IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO MAY ASK ABOUT IT.** At 711 a door off a third court that had been used eleven times in eight days has a rate, and the rate is not a count of claims and not a count of people. At 713 a Bureau officer serves nine returns on nine people at nine doors, discovers that **eight of them cannot find the office they had all handed paper to**, writes the last one down the only way the Bureau can write it, and carries it up two flights to a passage with no door onto a street. At 720 the man who has made all of this findable enters an instruction that every piece of paper received is to be entered as received **together with a description of the person who brought it**, and a clerk who may only enter what she is given enters it exactly, and the first row under it says *off the third court, the one with the stair at the back*, which is not an address and cannot be corrected and cannot be taken out.

**WHAT IT CLOSES: the possibility that anything in this Register is ever only about paper again. WHAT IT COSTS: about four hundred people are in a book in a building with no door onto a street, described in somebody else's words, and the only person in Ostara who may ask that office one question about any of it is him.**

all, and cannot say that anybody took anything off her** · **a ward, a shut door, a cot, nine minutes, and nothing there to take** · **a yard with nothing on the shutter since the ninth of November and a woman saying into an empty wall that she is not going to stand there and be a person about it** · **the chaplain asking how many people are in the yard this morning and saying that she has said four hundred on those steps for sixteen months and that it is not four hundred** · **a figure kept nine years on a woman's fingers, said out loud in a room for the first time, and said back badly by the woman who kept it** · **a bundle containing a sheet of paper with nothing written on it that came nine miles through a front door** · **a man behind a counter who has run it nine years and has never once asked anybody what a page was for, asking** · **sixty-two monthly forms stacked in a wall and the first rubbing ever made there** · **a department that answers elsewhere, a schedule with nothing in it about two words, and a slip the size of a thumb-nail which is not a way of getting anything and is a way of being found** · **a sentence said wrong about forty times inside an hour at the foot of a wall and corrected, which is the only thing this city has ever done to one of his sentences that worked.**

**THE VOLUME'S LAST IRREVERSIBLE DECISION IS AT 644 AND IT IS HIS.** **WHAT IT CLOSES:** the option of the fourth line — *and it is not on a page anywhere in this city* — standing in any yard, on any board, in any hand, for ever. It cannot be restored: a clerk may only enter what she is given and cannot improve it, an entry can be made and an entry cannot be taken back, and the page that carries the striking goes out at four on the thirtieth and about nine people a week will ever look at it. **WHAT IT COSTS:** every claim that rested on it dies at once, and the only one that mattered was always going to be a claim by a person who cannot read; about nine hundred people who can read a shutter know exactly who took it off; and he is the man who wrote the sentence that made it untestable in the first place. **WHAT IT IS NOT:** a scene, a rescue, a promotion, a defeat of Emil Brack, a climb, or an ending, and **he is still rank one on a branch night shift and nothing in this batch moves his hours, his plate, his quarters or his standing.**

**REFUSED:** the figure of the account · any floor, ledger total or running balance in grains · `settl` in every inflection · the reach of the return, argued by nobody in either direction · whether the fourth condition was ever true of anybody's deed · either repainting box · the keeper's six words · who put the white tile up · who cut the two words · Perrin Sowe · Dagmar Oyelowo · **any verbatim printing of the invented-figures sentence in 641-650. **DELIVERED:** a division that reads every paper twice and never compares the two readings, so the first number in this volume nobody can check is the seventeen between a round book and a desk book standing four feet apart, and a woman who counts ninety-one people a quarter on her fingers and will not write it down · **a landlord's man who asks for the fourth line to be put back on a board and is right about every fact including the one that costs him, and who came to be refused** · **the scene, at half past five on a returns desk with nine counters shut behind it, a woman who spends the only question a desk is allowed to spend on a question about a return, and says out loud that she has wanted him since the seventh of March and that there is no reason for it** · **a bar that is a bar: not one word of a demand says the person understood it, and if she were given every courtesy in the world and it did not help her, there would be nothing to touch her landlord** · **a proved standing that nobody in Ostara can strike, and the decision to be in a room with no standing in it on the fifteenth of September** · **the oldest ledger in a division, nineteen years old, and a rule that numbers in that building can only grow, and the discovery that the rule is not his** · **a woman who decides to stop counting a number she has carried for four years, and gives the reason herself** · **the yard's three lines and its nine hundred readers, and the third of them dying in a room in nine minutes, correctly, and a woman saying the first of them out loud in a corridor for the first time in six years** · **a man in a delivery coat who comes up a stair for the first time in three years to have the sentence in the office's hand read aloud, and who is told it stays because it is in your hand and not because it is right** · **the twenty-third sheet at four with the head unmoved for the seventh quarter, the office at sixty-seven months and twenty-nine days, a bundle of five things and a letter asking the office to correct a number** · **THE HILL: eight hundred and fifty-two said out loud twice, nine hundred hearers, two hundred hands, eleven minutes, CLAIMS, and a sentence taken down** · **a boy of sixteen who asks in six years what the two words are for, and is told, and works out in four seconds that he has known it since he was eleven** · **and a figure box left blank on purpose, and a man with a pencil and a ledger writing a date on a piece of paper because he has a pencil and no form about anything.**

## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, AND WHAT IT REFUSED

**DELIVERED:** the seam, and a quarter of a year of claims naming the office, and a bundle of four things that goes into a room in that building nobody can name · **the seam's answer, at a counting house: a broker who states her own position may not unstate it, six hundred and eighty entries that cannot be closed, and a real book of her own with one entry in it that has been carried four years** · **the scene, in the middle of a morning, a book squared and not opened, a woman who has not put a hand on anybody for four years, and the arithmetic said out loud and unable to be taken back** · the standing sheet with two lines in the second column and what the second one has been doing since the first of May · the yard's week, nine hundred readers, ten thousand who cannot read, and a man reading four lines out loud twice with nothing improved · the twenty-second sheet at four with the head unmoved for the sixth quarter running, the office at sixty-four months and twenty-nine days, and the bundle going into a room nobody can open · **the turn: about nine hundred people take the fourth line off a board themselves, one at a time, over about eleven minutes, with a rag and a bucket, and the man who wrote it is not asked, and the chaplain is not there and nobody goes up to her** · **the consequences, at a wall end at ten to six in the morning: about forty people in a lane, a man reading the margin of twelve books out loud for nothing, and a landlord's man with about nine demands** · **a yard with a rule and three lines on it, and about four hundred people all day, and a woman at the bottom of the hill who has walked from the other side of the city** · **and a woman in number four who cannot read, who wants a year of money she already won in January back on a board, and is told no by a man who cannot put it back because he wrote it into a book against himself on the fifteenth of October of the fourth year.**

**THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE DECISION IS AT 627 AND HE MAKES IT BY DOING NOTHING, AND 630 IS WHERE THE COST ARRIVES.** **WHAT IT CLOSES:** the option of putting the fourth line back on any board in any hand, for ever. **WHAT IT COSTS:** about nine hundred people in a yard have decided that he took it off himself, he cannot correct them, and eleven seconds later a woman he has watched from the foot of a stair since January asks him for the one thing in this city he has spent five years arranging not to be asked for. **WHAT IT IS NOT:** a scene, a rescue, a promotion, and **it is not the volume's last irreversible decision, which is at 644 and is his and is a pen and not a rag.**

# VOLUME 13 BATCH 0002 IS ON DISK. CHAPTERS 611–620 ARE WRITTEN PROSE. **TEN FINISHED FILES, 26,131 WORDS COUNTED PER FILE AND SUMMED BY COMMAND. MOVEMENT TWO, *ASKED*. THE SCENE AT 613 IS SUN MEILING'S — 550 CHAPTERS AFTER HER LAST ONE AND 10 CHAPTERS AFTER THE LAST SCENE IN THE BOOK. THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE DECISION IS AT 611 AND IT IS HIS: HE SAYS HIS OWN NAME INTO A FINDING. THE MOVEMENT'S TURN IS AT 620 AND IT IS NOT HIS: A YARD HAS A WEEK AND HE IS KEPT OUT OF IT BY A WOMAN WHO ASKED HIM FOR NOTHING. THE PAYMENT VOLUME 12 OWED IS AT 615 AND 617 AND IT IS MADE BY EMIL BRACK AND NOT BY LIN HAO. `outline/ending.md` IS UNTOUCHED. NO VOLUME-CLOSE PROMPT, NO BATCH 0004, AND `state/complete.md` IS NOT CREATED. THE ONE NEXT PHASE IS `workspace/volume-13/batch-0003/PROMPT.md`, CHAPTERS 621–630, MOVEMENT THREE, *OWED*.** THIS BLOCK SUPERSEDES EVERY BLOCK BELOW IT AND DELETES NONE OF THEM.

## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, AND WHAT IT REFUSED

**DELIVERED:** the office named in a finding for the first time in six years because a landlord swore where he copied the four lines from, and a magistrate's clerk entitled to one question which is *who wrote those four lines*, and a man who spent six years arranging not to be found saying his own name into a record · **a copy of the standing page copied into that file**, and a Registrar telling him he has handed the office a second address, and that the thing he was protecting against was never compulsion but being read · nine divisions returning nine lines to a finding and Beatrix Halm, deaf in one ear, asking what the two-inch space is for, and his own sentence going out in her hand to a magistrate · **the scene, two floors under a sales floor, a folder taken in the order it was opened, a woman asked for the sixth time and answering inside two seconds, and a question at the end of it that nobody in this city can answer** · the twenty-first sheet at four with the head unmoved for the fifth time running, the office at sixty-one months and twenty-nine days, the lane at one thousand nine hundred and seventy-eight mornings, both printed once with operands · a desk under a window and two mornings of a woman who cannot read standing at it · **a real book entry that a page can shut wrongly, shown on a second unsealed book a keeper has had in that room since long before there was anything in it, and shown to nobody** · **the payment, in a lane at ten to seven in the morning: a woman told that a figure about her was never hers, that nobody ever told her, and that there is no way in this city of knowing whether a thing written down is true — and given nothing** · four sentences at the foot of a page read aloud in order by the man entitled to read them, and a minute of his own going in front of a magistrate · **a second demand with four lines and no address, carried across a city at eleven at night** · **a hall booked for a week, and a woman of rank two who came to tell him about it and asked him for nothing.**

**THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE DECISION IS AT 611 AND IT IS HIS. WHAT IT CLOSES:** six years of having no author on anything — a rule with no author cannot be argued with, and that was the only defence he built. **WHAT IT COSTS:** his name in a document a magistrate will turn over, a copy of the office's own page inside that document, and a clerk telling him to his face that there is not one person in this city who can give him anything for it. He wanted, for about four seconds, to be a man who had not been asked. **WHAT IT IS NOT:** a scene, a rescue, a promotion, and it is not the volume's last irreversible decision, which is at 644.

**REFUSED:** the figure of the account · any floor, ledger total or running balance in grains · `settle` in every inflection · the reach of the return, argued by nobody in either direction · whether the fourth condition was ever true of anybody's deed · either repainting box · the keeper's six words · who put the white tile up · Perrin Sowe · Dagmar Oyelowo · Hanneke Ruis, who is furniture in 613 and is given no age and no mark and is not a person in it · **Mavis Rooke's hand-flat, and no hand flat on a table anywhere in the ten** · a second conversation with the man with the broom · **a second time up the two flights off Cordwain, and the stair is not used** · **the identity of the woman paying a quarter into a book at the Vant, which belongs to 623 and is NOT merged with the woman on the ninth line down** · Brack thanked, diminished, defeated or wrong about any fact · **either four hundred's figure, and the four four-hundreds that do stand in these ten files are named and classified at §0c** · any day of the week · any announced age · any year numeral in the prose · any mark, temple, eye or ink for Sun Meiling, Mavis Rooke or Hanneke Ruis · a fourth-wall hit, including `manuscript` and `opposition` · any system panel · a second verbatim printing of the invented-figures sentence · anything in `outline/ending.md`, which this phase did not touch.

## 0z. WHAT THIS BATCH DELIVERED, AND WHAT IT REFUSED

**DELIVERED:** a demand with four lines on it and *is there* written in pencil on the back, put on a table by a clerk and gone again · three correct refusals in a row and an answer that is a sentence the office printed to be true, written four times a year, that nobody in the room wrote down · **the scene, in a corridor and a stairwell of a branch building at eleven at night, with a Bureau field officer of rank two who cannot serve a man who has no standing and serves him by hand up two flights and writes down that she did** · a woman who cannot read being paid nine years of short money off a sentence she will never see, and asking who wrote the four lines · three women on a rota and one of them understanding the sentence at the foot for the first time and saying she is not going to say anything about it · about nine hundred people in a yard working out that the fourth line cannot be tested by anybody · a real book in a building off Cordwain that cannot close an entry for exactly that reason, and a sum going into a book that is not that book once a quarter by a person four floors up who does not know it was called · a department of works, a form, and a wall that comes down in the spring · the man with the chalk told that the office has made him legal and wanting nothing · **and two flights of a dark stair with nobody on the landing at the top of them.**

**THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE DECISION IS AT 610 AND IT IS HIS. WHAT IT CLOSES:** the option of being the man who did not go up, which he said on a street in the fifth year and again to himself at four in the morning with a tally board across his knees, and meant both times, and had been quietly proud of. **WHAT IT COSTS:** an hour of the night shift coming on at eleven, a morning he had not meant to spend, and **the certainty that he could still be careful**, which was the last thing he owned that nobody could take off him by wanting something. **WHAT IT IS NOT:** a scene, a rescue, an opening of anything. He gets nothing, there is nobody at the top of the stairs, and he does not knock, because a knock is a thing a man does when he wants something and he did not want something. **AND NO CHAPTER OF 611–650 GOES UP THOSE TWO FLIGHTS A SECOND TIME.** Carried at `state/open-threads.md`.

**REFUSED:** the figure of the account · any floor, ledger total or running balance in grains · `settle` in every inflection · the reach of the return, argued by nobody in either direction · whether the fourth condition was ever true of anybody's deed · either repainting box · the keeper's six words · who put the white tile up · Perrin Sowe · Dagmar Oyelowo · Hanneke Ruis, who is not in this batch at all · any year numeral · any announced age · any mark for Runa Sato, Mavis Rooke or Hanneke Ruis · **Mavis Rooke's hand-flat** · a second conversation with the man with the broom, who is not in this batch · Brack thanked, diminished, defeated or wrong about any fact · **either four hundred** — `chapter-0545.md:87`'s four hundred a day and `chapter-0500.md:35`'s four hundred since the first of January are not printed, derived or mentioned anywhere in 601–610 · any day of the week · any new enemy · **any second time on the second of January, the eighth of October or the tenth of October, and no chapter of 601–610 lands on any of the three** · a fourth-wall hit · anything in `outline/ending.md`, which this phase did not touch.

## 0y. THE SIX FINDINGS, WHAT WAS WRONG, AND WHAT EACH ONE NOW SAYS

**1 (APPLIED, IN THREE FILES) · THE VOLUME'S PREMISE HAD THE FOUR CONDITIONS ENTERED A YEAR LATE, IN THE ONE SENTENCE THE WHOLE VOLUME IS BUILT ON.** `chapters/volume-11/chapter-0548.md:121` reads *the fifteenth of October of the fourth year*, and `:9` reads *the first of October of the fourth year*. `state/current.md` §0b, `outline/volume-13.md` §7 and the Volume 13 row of `state/chapter-summaries.md` all said **the fifth year**. `3 × 360 + 240 + 14 = 1,334`, and chapter 548 is that day. **NOW: the fourth year, the column headed carried by, the fifteenth of October, and `1,773 − 1,334 = 439` days is how long it has gone unspoken.** The row also said *in six years*, which could not be true of an event in year four measured in year six, and that phrase is gone rather than replaced.

**2 (APPLIED) · *THE ORDINARY REPAINTING FORM* IS NOT ON THE PAGE, AND IT IS THE OBJECT A STANDING PROHIBITION GUARDS.** `chapter-0548.md` contains no *form*, no *box* and no *repaint*, verified by command with a control grep that works; the claim went into **the column headed carried by**, entered exactly as given by a clerk who may only enter. **THE TWO REPAINTING BOXES ARE A DIFFERENT RECURRING OBJECT AND ARE BLANK FOR EVER UNDER §2c, AND A BATCH THAT INHERITED *THE FORM* WOULD HAVE HAD A STANDING PROHIBITION AND AN ENTRY IN THE SAME SENTENCE.** Corrected in `state/current.md` §0b and `outline/volume-13.md` §2b, where the repair is recorded in the file itself.

**3 (APPLIED) · *HE WROTE THEM IN FORTY DAYS* BORROWSED THE DEFINITION'S FIGURE AND GAVE IT TO THE CONDITIONS.** `chapter-0548.md:7` says *he wrote it in about eleven seconds*, and the page adds *five days from the tenth of October to this morning*. **THE FORTY DAYS AND THE KITCHEN ON THE NINETEENTH OF JULY OF YEAR TWO BELONG TO THE DEFINITION OF AN UNRECORDED DEED, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT EVENT ON A DIFFERENT DATE, AND THE TWO ARE NOW SEPARATED IN `outline/volume-13.md` §2b, IN THE PREMISE SENTENCE AND IN CARD 601.** Neither figure was invented; both were attached to the wrong page.

## 0b. THE THREE DECISIONS IN `outline/volume-13.md` THAT A LATER PHASE MUST NOT REVERSE

**1 · THE VOLUME'S OBJECT IS THE FOURTH OF HIS FOUR CONDITIONS.** He entered the four conditions against himself, in his own hand, **in the column headed carried by, on the fifteenth of October of the fourth year**, having spent five days deciding and having written the four lines in about eleven seconds — `chapter-0548.md:121`, on the page. **Three of the four were met and the fourth was not**, and the clerk gave the reason in one sentence: the thing it describes is on a page in this city. **Nobody has said it out loud in a room since, and `1,773 − 1,334 = 439` days is how long.** The fourth line is *and it is not on a page anywhere in this city*, and since the ninth of November of year five the office has printed, in its own hand, that a figure in Ostara may be a figure somebody made up on purpose. **The volume's question is whether the fourth line survives its own author, and the volume's last irreversible decision is at 644: he strikes it out of his own hand, in the office's hand, on the office's own standing page, with his own name under the striking, and writes nothing in its place.**

*(REPAIRED 14 OCTOBER 2026 AGAINST `logs/next-0004.review.log`, FINDINGS 1 AND 2. THIS ROW SAID **THE ORDINARY REPAINTING FORM** AND **IN THE FIFTH YEAR**, AND NEITHER IS ON THE PAGE. The four conditions went into the column headed *carried by*, not onto a form; the two repainting boxes are a different recurring object and are blank for ever, and naming one where the page names the other would have invited a batch to write the entry as a form. The year was the fourth, and "in six years" could not be right either — the entry is year four and this volume is year six. `chapter-0548.md` was not edited.)*

**2 · THREE OF THE FIVE THREADS VOLUME 12 DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN ARE HANDED ON AND ONE IS PAID.** `reviews/volume-12/volume-close.md` §11 handed two: *whether the woman two flights up ever learns*, and *what comes off the shelf on the first of January*. **The second one is a keeper's book that came off the shelf in Volume 12 at 553 and 554 and is spent. The first one is the Register's first creditor and Volume 13 closes it in movement two, at 615 and 617, made by Emil Brack and not by Lin Hao, and not as a scene and not as a gift.** Volume 13 opens exactly one thread of its own: **a form from the department of works says the ranks wall comes down in the spring for making good, and two words that have survived six years of monthly repainting are on the stone.**

**3 · THE HOUSE FORM IS SETTLED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN A PLANNING FILE.** `reviews/volume-12/volume-close.md` Finding B: **1,540 straight quote glyphs in 551–570, 0 in 571–600, 35,895 across Volumes 01–11.** A gate that measures only its own ten files cannot see a change made between batches, and that is how four arithmetic gates passed a house-form change. **THE FIRST TWO FIGURES RE-DERIVE EXACTLY. ## 0a. OPEN ITEM 5, JUDGED — AND THIS AUDIT DISAGREES WITH THE DEFENCE

Batch 0005 disclosed that eight of ten chapters sit below the 1,800 guide floor, that three consecutive batches have breached it, and defended it: *nothing was padded, because these chapters are short because they are one afternoon or one street, and padding them would be the worse defect.*

**The disclosure is honest. The defence does not survive measurement, and the close prompt asked for a judgement rather than a disclosure.**

**THE EXCHANGE COLUMN IS RENAMED AND ITS METHOD IS NOW DECLARED, BECAUSE THE FIRST EDITION OF THIS TABLE DECLARED THE PARAGRAPH COLUMN'S METHOD AND NOT ITS OWN.** *Quoted spans* is every double-quoted run of non-newline text, **either glyph**, per file, summed over the movement and divided by ten; it must be glyph-neutral, because 551–570 carry 770 straight spans and no curly and 571–600 carry no straight span and 542 curly, so a straight-only probe reads zero for the last three movements and a curly-only probe reads zero for the first two. *Paragraphs* is every non-blank line that is neither a `##` heading nor an italic footer, divided by ten: 542 · 668 · 280 · 394 · 328, and 564 = 150 and 584 = 68 confirm it. **THE REPAIR PASS AGAINST THE REVIEW OF `reviews/volume-12/volume-close.md` RE-DERIVED THE EXCHANGE COLUMN: the figures printed here as 7.9 / 8.5 / 10.2 re-derive from nothing and are 16.1 / 17.4 / 20.7. THE WORD COLUMN AND THE PARAGRAPH COLUMN WERE RIGHT, ARE RESTORED UNCHANGED, AND THE WORD COLUMN STANDS COUNTED PER FILE AND SUMMING 93,730.** Full working at §13 of that audit, including the near-miss this repair pass made on the paragraph column before catching it.

**Volume 12's mean is 1,874 words — the lowest of any volume in the book, 152 below Volume 9 and roughly 400 below Volumes 1–8 and 11. Twenty-five of its fifty chapters are below the floor, the worst count in the manuscript.** But the word count is not the finding. **The finding is that dramatic density fell at chapter 571 and never recovered.** Movement two's quarter-end runs 28 quoted spans across 51 paragraphs; movement five's runs 10 across 32. Movement two's scene has 129 spans and 150 paragraphs; movement four's has 32 and 68. **The fall is 3.2 times measured from movement two and 1.5 times measured from movement one, not the factor of four to six the first edition of this table claimed. A measure that changes value where the typography changes must not be used to diagnose what changed there, which is the second reason the earlier figure is withdrawn.**

**THE UNIT SIZES DID NOT CHANGE.** `chapter-0562.md` is one court room and one counter: 48 paragraphs, 2,091 words, 22 quoted spans. `chapter-0588.md` is one passage and one pencil: 31 paragraphs, 1,477 words, 11 quoted spans. **In words the two rooms are within half again of each other; in quoted spans it is exactly two to one, and the difference is not the room.** What changed at 571 is the form.

I checked the last chapter against its card to be sure the beats were present. **They are.** `chapter-0600.md` carries every promise — the empty tray, 852 unmoved, the sheet out at four, ninety days and one year and half a year with their operands, the lane's 1,888 mornings printed once, the office at fifty-eight months and twenty-nine days, the verdict in his own hand, Brack not defeated, the tile unnamed, January shut like a chained book. **Nothing is missing. Everything is shorter than it needed to be, and it is short because it is told rather than lived.**

**THE VERDICT: nothing was padded and nothing should have been, and that half of the defence stands. But leanness is not compression, and the volume's last thirty chapters are compressed.** No plot beat is missing. It is a book that stops dramatising halfway through itself. **Recorded as a judgement about a closed volume, with the numbers, so that a later planner inherits it as a fact and not as a mood.**

## 1. WHERE THE MAN STANDS AT 571, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, FROM THE PAGE

He is at rank one on a branch night shift he asked for, eleven at night until half past five, four nights and three off, a white plate with his name on it and no figure cut into it anywhere. **On the fourth of February a landlord told him to his face that he is behind and has been behind since the thirtieth of December, and that there will be four hundred of his own printed demands in that district by the middle of the month and every one of them is a conversation the landlord does not have to have with a man in a coat.** **On the seventeenth he stood at the back of a room off a court and watched nine people come to a counter, and four of them got all the way to the fourth of his four lines and all four had nothing, and a clerk in a clerk's coat wrote *nothing proved* in the box where the proof goes, four times, in his own hand, and has no choice about it.** **On the twenty-eighth of February a keeper two floors under a sales floor said a figure out loud for the first time in thirty years and would not write it down, and he carried it up two flights and gave it to a woman who keeps a list and works for nobody, and there are now two copies of a hundred and twenty in this city and neither is certified.** **On the ninth of March a chaplain sent for him for the first time in four years, and went out and stood in front of about eleven thousand people and said one thing and nobody answered her, because about nine hundred people in that yard have learned from her that the way to be heard by a crowd is not to be answered, and she lost the room, which was the only place in this city where a thing said in public comes back through a door where it cannot be used.** **On the nineteenth of March a compositor who has set type for nineteen years read his four lines upside down and worked out that the fourth one is the door and the other three are the list and that you cannot get through a door by holding the list, and nobody asked him, and he took his own name off his own plate and printed about eight hundred copies over two nights, and the fourth condition is on all of them.** **On the thirtieth the figure at the head of the sheet moved for the first time in four quarters, from eight hundred and forty-one to eight hundred and fifty-two, because eleven people wrote their own accounts on the back of a printed sheet and sent them to the address at the head of a public page, and no division went for them and nobody asked anybody anything, and the second column still had one line in it and the line was him.** **On the eighth of April a man who loads coal at a wharf told him he has asked about two hundred and forty people his four questions at the foot of the yard steps and written every answer down, and that he has not brought any of them in, and that he will not.** **On the seventeenth a woman who keeps a lodging house and reads everything twice put about a hundred and thirty-nine names on the back of a printed sheet in her own hand in one night, on purpose, and handed them to the woman who keeps the list, and refused to use him once.** **On the thirtieth his own Registrar refused to have his name or this office's mark at the top of a notice in nine division corridors, and the woman who keeps the list carried the page to a room off a third court with no sign on the door, and a clerk put it in the drawer that has been open and empty since the fourth of February of the first year and shut a drawer that was already shut.** **And on the first of May he read his own four lines on a board at thirty feet in a Bureau corridor with no name on them, and went to a room off a third court, and wrote four lines in his own hand and entered the first name on the yard's board against himself in the column headed *carried by*, without asking her one question, and it cannot be struck, and on the thirtieth of June it goes out on a public page with his name against hers.**

## 2. WHAT THIS BATCH OWED AND DELIVERED

- **561 — a landlord who is right, four hundred printed demands, three copies given away to strangers, and the arithmetic of a finding, which is one thousand four hundred and forty days and is not eviction and is worse.**

## 3. THE IRREVERSIBLE DECISION THIS BATCH OWES, AND IT IS 570, AND IT IS HIS

**HE ENTERS THE FIRST NAME ON THE YARD'S BOARD IN THE COLUMN HEADED *CARRIED BY*, IN HIS OWN HAND, AGAINST HIMSELF, IN FOUR LINES WRITTEN EXACTLY IN THE SHAPE OF THE FOUR LINES HE ENTERED AGAINST HIMSELF ON THE FIFTEENTH OF OCTOBER.** He had not asked her anything. He had never seen her. He cannot strike it, because a clerk may only enter what she is given and cannot improve it and cannot be asked to hurry, and there is no form in this city for striking a line a person entered against themselves in their own hand.

**WHAT IT CLOSES:** the option of being a man who kept a book of deeds, which he said out loud in a yard on the thirtieth of January and about nine hundred people in that yard told him he was wrong about, and the option of the second column having exactly one line in it for ever. **WHAT IT COSTS:** he has done, in ink and in his own hand, the exact thing he described at half past eleven on the thirtieth of January as the failure of his own definition — a person found without being asked — and about nine in ten of the hundred and thirty-nine people on that page are people the four conditions throw out, and he has entered her anyway, and she is not going to be told, because there is no instrument for telling her, and she cannot read a page.

## 0. WHERE THE MAN STANDS AT 561, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, FROM THE PAGE

He is at rank one on a branch night shift he asked for, eleven at night until half past five, four nights and three off, a white plate with his name on it and no figure cut into it anywhere. **On the thirtieth of December the sixteenth sheet went out at four with his name at the head of one line in the second column and about four hundred and eighteen other people's words underneath it, and a sentence underneath that which he did not write. On the first of January a keeper chained a book two floors under a sales floor with his name on a page in it. On the second of January she read it, asked him the question she had carried for eleven years, spent it on him, and then took him against a table in a cold room and told him she wanted it before she had it. On the seventh a copy of three of his four conditions went up on the branch's own corridor notice board with a drawing pin through it and the fourth line gone. On the tenth the four lines were in four-inch chalk on a shutter at the yard end with a true notice naming the quarter and the Bureau. On the thirteenth a yard of about eleven thousand had decided in four minutes that the board is a rule and not a quotation, and the new word in that yard is *asked for*. On the sixteenth a woman he had never met stood six feet off him in about nine hundred people and asked whether the four lines on that board are the ones he wrote, and he said yes, out loud, in his own voice, and could not un-say it. On the twenty-first a landlord put the four lines into a demand and he let it stand, because a person who cannot produce a deed has not proved anything and he wrote a rule that says so. On the thirtieth he told eleven thousand people his name was on it, and when the woman who has been in that yard for nine years asked him what he was going to do about the people the four lines leave out, he said nothing, twice, and it was the truth. The Register is now a book of names and not a book of deeds and he is the man standing in the yard who made it that way. A column of about a hundred names in the yard's own chalk is going down the wall under the four lines and not one of the four conditions will take any of them.**

## 1. THE FIGURE ERROR THIS BATCH FOUND, AND IT WAS IN THE BRIEF

**`workspace/volume-12/batch-0001/PROMPT.md` §2 gave chapter 559 as spine day 1,433, AND 1,433 IS THE TWENTY-FOURTH OF JANUARY, NOT THE TWENTY-FIRST.** The date is fixed by `outline/volume-12.md` §5c's table and is 21 January. Re-derived twice by methods that share no constant: `(y-2) × 360 + 330 + (d-1)` = `3 × 360 + 330 + 20` = **1,430**; and counted back from 1 February of year five = `4 × 360 = 1,440`, whose preceding day is 30 January = 1,439, and `1,439 − (30 − 21)` = 1,439 − 9 = **1,430**. Both agree.

**TWO INTERVALS IN THE BRIEF WERE CONSEQUENTLY WRONG AND BOTH ARE NOW RIGHT ON THE PAGE: 558→559 is 1,430 − 1,425 = 5 days and not eight, and 559→560 is 1,439 − 1,430 = 9 days and not six.** 1,430 − 1,240 = **190 days** since the eleventh of July of year four, not 193, and 190 = 6 × 30 + 10. **THE BRIEF'S OWN RULE IS WHAT CAUGHT IT — *a figure nobody re-computes is the figure that is wrong* — and the run that caught it is the run the standing instruction asks for, which is twice from the two formulas, never copied out of a chapter.** The correction is recorded in `outline/volume-12.md` §5c and the day number is now 1,430 in every state row and in both chapters.

## WHERE HE STANDS AT 551, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, FROM THE PAGE

He is at rank one on a branch night shift he asked for, eleven at night until half past five, four nights and three off, a white plate with his name on it and no figure cut into it anywhere, and the rota page at that branch now carries four names on it. The Register of Unrecorded Merit has been open forty-one months and ten days as counted off the first of February of the first year, has a room with two chairs and a drawer that has been open and empty since the fourth of February of that year, and a book in which the second column, ruled on the ninth of March of the third year, was empty for seven quarter-ends (**561 days at the thirtieth of September of year four — 1,319 − 758 — and 576 at the fifteenth of October — 1,334 − 758; REPAIRED 14 OCTOBER 2026, it printed *five quarters* on eight lines**) and has one line in it. **That line is his.** On the fifteenth of October he entered, in his own hand and entered exactly as given by a clerk who may only enter, a claim against himself: that the thing returned on the first of October was taken from about a million people and that he decided who received it. Of the four conditions, three were met and the fourth was not, and the reason is that the thing it describes is on a page in this city. It cannot be struck. It goes out on a public desk on the thirtieth of December. A woman who dug a street for six years and was never paid is the Register's first creditor and she is two flights up off Cordwain, and **he is never going to tell her, and the page will — whether she ever reads that page is open and is carried to the next volume.** A street four streets off the yard end that has been counted four times in thirty years was read once in ninety days and every person it found lost the fourth condition of his own definition. The Church has about eleven thousand in its yard, a column it intends to fill, and a chaplain who has lost it. Emil Brack's offer — every figure he has invented, the method, and nine he decided off nothing, for one line in the office's hand saying he makes them up — **is unanswered and he is undefeated and he is right about every fact.** The slates are still in a lane off Cordwain, the wall still cannot be read by anybody, and the white tile under the last tile still has his name on it in chalk and nothing whatever under it, and nobody in this city has put it there.

## 0. WHERE THE MAN STANDS AT CHAPTER 531, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, FROM THE PAGE

He is at rank one on a branch night shift he asked for, eleven at night until half past five, a white plate with his name on it and no figure cut into it anywhere. ## 2. THE TWO IRREVERSIBLE DECISIONS THIS BATCH OWNS, AND BOTH ARE HIS

**525. HE ENTERS A FIGURE AGAINST THE WOMAN WHO GAVE IT TO HIM'S EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION.** A street and a figure and no name, on the twenty-seventh of January, entered by a clerk who read it twice at the same speed both times and asked him nothing.

An office called the Register of Unrecorded Merit has a room off a third court with two chairs and a table in it, and for eight months two people came to that door, and it has taken a sentence from him that is four lines long and has a threshold in it: a deed is unrecorded if all four of four things are true of it, and it excludes about nine in ten of what people will bring, and he said the number out loud in a kitchen and did not explain it. ## 0. WHERE HE STANDS AT THE END OF CHAPTER 500, IN ONE PARAGRAPH, FROM THE PAGE

On the eighth of October an office painted two words and a dash and two more words along the foot of the ranks wall at six in the morning, out of a repainting form, in a clerk's hand, and no person in Ostara has ever found out what it means. For two days Cordwain tried to decide whether the wall had been lying for thirty years, and Agnete Lindqvist read the line, said it was the Church's four words with the hand cut off, and refused to claim it. On the tenth he stood in a room that could carry nothing with ninety people in it and asked them to keep the Bureau, and a keeper of the Vant's real books read him the best case anybody in that room had heard, and he refused to argue for or against the first of October in front of them, and the minute went out at four with an address at the head of every line, and from that afternoon the Bureau of Merit survives on a sentence a man with no standing said in a room, and he has said out loud that it is his position and not the Board's merit and that he will not go back outside the door. On the seventeenth of October nine sworn women sat at one table in a kitchen off Ferrier Street, each of them said one thing and nobody answered anybody, and the ninth said hers last and the room agreed with her, and three of them have not slept in that house since the first of October and all three of them are on the December rota at his branch. On the twenty-fourth a carter off Lamplit Row was told at a public desk that his file is not lost and that nobody in this city can find it. On the thirtieth a keeper two floors under a sales floor set out four times a year for thirty years in one hand and said that the rule which has always been a defect is now the only thing standing. On the thirtieth of November he did not ask the three why they had gone and said out loud that he never will. On the first of January he cleaned washrooms from eleven at night until half past five because rank one gets assigned work and because he asked, a woman he has been living beside for four years filed a correction on the twenty-ninth of December and did not press it and neither of them said one word about what was in it, three women came in on the rota and worked, and on a wall two streets away there is a white tile with his name on it in chalk and nothing under it. On the fourteenth a woman read the second line on the wall, came down to a counter and asked whether she could put a thing she did in a doorway into a form, and he told her she cannot, and spent ninety seconds looking for her on a page of four hundred clock times and could not find her. And on the twenty-eighth of January he read the standing sheet of the quarter of the thirtieth of December at a public desk, and under the disposition there was one figure in a clerk's hand, and it is two hundred and eleven thousand, eight hundred and forty grains, and about one in seven of everything that went out on the first of October did not go anywhere, and it is not zero, and it belongs to nobody, and it will be on a page again on the thirtieth of March in a woman's handwriting under her own name.

## 2. THE BATCH'S IRREVERSIBLE DECISIONS, AND THEY ARE BOTH HIS

**493, THE TENTH OF OCTOBER. HE DEFENDS THE BUREAU IN PUBLIC, AT RANK ONE, TO PEOPLE WHO WANTED IT BROKEN, AND HE SAYS OUT LOUD THAT ITS SURVIVAL IS NOW HIS POSITION AND NOT ITS OWN MERIT.**

**497, THE THIRTIETH OF NOVEMBER. HE DOES NOT ASK THE THREE WHY THEY HAVE LEFT AND HE NEVER ASKS.**
